column1: A patient presents with deep caries in one of his teeth. His dentist explains that the best treatment is a crown. He asks the dentist if he could do a filling. The dentist explains that a filling can be done but is not his best option as she does not know how long it will hold up. The patient insists that the dentist does the filling. The dentist performs the filling as the patient wants. This is an example of which of the following ethical principles?
column2: Autonomy
column3: Beneficence
column4: Non-maleficence
column5: Justice
column6: Veracity

column1: Consider the following three statements: I. It is unethical for a dentist to practice while abusing controlled substances, alcohol or other chemical agents that impair the ability to practice. II. All dentists have an ethical obligation to urge chemically-impaired colleagues to seek treatment. III. Dentists do not have an ethical responsibility to report evidence of an impaired colleague to the professional assistance committee of a dental society if that dentist does not self-report. Which of these statements are CONSISTENT WITH the ADA Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct?
column2: I, II, and III.
column3: I and II.
column4: I and III.
column5: II and III.
column6: None of these statements are CONSISTENT WITH the ADA Principles of Ethics and Code of Professional Conduct.

column1: Which of the following statements is FALSE?

column1: During lecture we discussed a case in which a corporate dental group made an unrestricted donation to a dental school in exchange for a faculty member from one of the six general dental clinics providing resumes and rankings of what he considered to be his top five students. This dental group decided not to participate in the school's job fair after they received this information. When considering this case, which of the following statements is FALSE?
column2: Having additional information such as whether students outside of these select five students could still apply for jobs may be helpful in deciding if this was an ethical practice.
column3: This was an acceptable practice because all of the students at the school had an equal chance of getting a recommendation from this faculty member.
column4: When evaluating this case in terms of ethics, it is important to consider the perspective of the school, the students, and the other dental practices participating in the job fair.
column5: The practice was not necessarily going to end up with the best dentist employees.
column6: The other dental practices participating in the job fair did not have the same opportunities to meet students as did this corporate dental group.

column1: Which of the following action violates the ethical principle of VERACITY?

column5: Advertising yourself as a “specialist” in a procedure when it is commonly done by all dentists with no special training or skills.
column6: All of the actions on this list violate the ethical principle of VERACITY.

column1: In the small group sessions we discussed a case in which a dentist was concerned that his patient who needed antibiotic prophylaxis would go to a different dentist and not receive the necessary antibiotic prior to dental treatment. The patient would not allow this dentist to inform the new dentist of the patient's condition and the need for antibiotic prophylaxis. Consider the following statements: I. The ethical principles of BENEFICENCE and NON-MALEFICENCE support the argument that the original dentist should inform the new dentist of the need for antibiotic prophylaxis. II. The ethical principle of AUTONOMY supports the argument that the original dentist should not inform the new dentist of the need for antibiotic prophylaxis.
column2: Both statements are TRUE.

column1: In the small group sessions we discussed a case in which a patient wanted their dentist to make a bridge on teeth that were not healthy enough to support the bridge. Which of the following statements is FALSE?

column4: A dentist may be ethically bound to refuse a patient's request for sub-standard care.

column6: A patient's right to autonomy takes precedent over all other ethical principles that may play a role in a dentist's decision-making.

column1: In the small group sessions we discussed a case in which an office manager changed a new dentist's treatment plans for simple restorations to more extensive crowns. Which of the following statements is TRUE?

column3: If the patient was not involved in the treatment decision-making process, including when the treatment plan was changed, this may be an illegal practice as patient informed consent was not obtained.
column4: Performing unnecessary services, including substituting a more extensive and subsequently more expensive and profitable procedure for a simpler, more effective and less expensive procedure, is an unethical practice.
column5: Performing unnecessary services, including substituting a more extensive and subsequently more expensive and profitable procedure for a simpler, more effective and less expensive procedure and billing this to an insurance company, may be an illegal practice, as this can be considered insurance fraud.
column6: All of these statements listed here are TRUE.
